method.manual: Native view_image of original source images, with local IIIF detail views of 1r; no OCR, no automated image-to-text, no image editing or image publication.
method.normalization: Expand standard abbreviations; normalize u/v, capitals and punctuation for readability; retain medieval e in celum/lune/sapientie/nate and source aptatione. No insertions from Wikisource or modern standard text.
method.notation: ⟨sicut⟩ is visible interlinear written correction, not conjectured text. Square brackets with ? mark unresolved readings/expansions; t[h?]elesmi preserves uncertain h. Source line divisions approximate the 17 visible main-text baselines; punctuation is editorial. ⟦...?⟧ records an apparently cancelled/overwritten, unresolved letter group between una and aptatione; it is not silently counted as an active word.
method.scope: This is a bounded manual reading, not a critical edition or diplomatic certified transcription. Complete semantic outline means no main-body clause was dropped, not every word resolved.

normalized_lines.reading: Philosophus dicit: Verum sine mendacio, certum verissimum. Quod est superius
est sicut quod est inferius, et quod est inferius est sicut quod est superius, ad
penetranda miracula unius rei. Sicut omnes res ab
uno fuerunt meditatione unius. Et ⟨sicut⟩ nate fuerunt res omnes
ab hac re una ⟦...?⟧ aptatione. Pater eius sol, mater eius
luna. Portavit illud ventus in ventre suo. Nutrix eius est terra.
Pater omnis t[h?]elesmi totius mundi est hic. Vis eius integra est
si versa fuerit in terram. Separabis terram ab igne, subtile a spisso,
suaviter[que?] cum magno ingenio. Ascendit a terra in celum, iterumque
descendit in terram et recipit vim superiorum et inferiorum. Sic
[habuit?] gloriam totius mundi. Ideoque fugiet a te omnis
obscuritas. Hic est totius mundi fortitudinis fortis
fortitudo, quia vincet omnem rem subtilem et omnem rem solidam
penetrabit. Sicut [ergo?] mundus creatus est. Hinc erunt apta-
tiones mirabiles, quarum [modus?] hic est. Itaque vocatus sum
Hermes, tres totius mundi partes habens sapientie. Completum
est quod dixi de operatione solis et lune.

normalized_complete_reading: Philosophus dicit: Verum sine mendacio, certum verissimum. Quod est superius est sicut quod est inferius, et quod est inferius est sicut quod est superius, ad penetranda miracula unius rei. Sicut omnes res ab uno fuerunt meditatione unius. Et ⟨sicut⟩ nate fuerunt res omnes ab hac re una ⟦...?⟧ aptatione. Pater eius sol, mater eius luna. Portavit illud ventus in ventre suo. Nutrix eius est terra. Pater omnis t[h?]elesmi totius mundi est hic. Vis eius integra est si versa fuerit in terram. Separabis terram ab igne, subtile a spisso, suaviter[que?] cum magno ingenio. Ascendit a terra in celum, iterumque descendit in terram et recipit vim superiorum et inferiorum. Sic [habuit?] gloriam totius mundi. Ideoque fugiet a te omnis obscuritas. Hic est totius mundi fortitudinis fortis fortitudo, quia vincet omnem rem subtilem et omnem rem solidam penetrabit. Sicut [ergo?] mundus creatus est. Hinc erunt aptationes mirabiles, quarum [modus?] hic est. Itaque vocatus sum Hermes, tres totius mundi partes habens sapientie. Completum est quod dixi de operatione solis et lune.

uncertainty_apparatus.evidence: The upper red rubric is only partially read here. Its intervening word is not securely transcribed. It is not silently supplied from a catalogue title.
uncertainty_apparatus.semantic_limit: Not part of the following 17-line body; no invented title Tabula smaragdina claimed as written rubric.

uncertainty_apparatus.evidence: No independent et is confidently visible between these two words. The reading therefore does not supply the familiar extra conjunction.
uncertainty_apparatus.semantic_limit: No material effect on truth-assertion content; a real transcription distinction.

uncertainty_apparatus.evidence: Preferred native reading penetranda. The letter sequence and a repetition in 1v support this over the familiar perpetranda. No edition-based substitution made.
uncertainty_apparatus.semantic_limit: Opening infinitival purpose and later penetrabit may share the penetrate verb family; the abstract object miracula does not force a literal physical penetration.

uncertainty_apparatus.evidence: Sicut is visibly supplied above the line after Et, with overwritten/cancelled lower writing. The cancelled letters are not securely reconstructed. Nate is the preferred following reading. Commentary 1v has the corresponding lemma with fuerunt nate order.
uncertainty_apparatus.semantic_limit: The corrected reading is represented, while the prior scribal state remains unresolved. No invented clean uncorrected et sicut line.

uncertainty_apparatus.evidence: The contracted form is expanded meditatione, also supported by the 1v lemma. It is not normalized to mediatione.
uncertainty_apparatus.semantic_limit: Meditation/thought or mediation is not automatically a laboratory operation; the precise philosophical sense and referent of unius remain open.

uncertainty_apparatus.evidence: Preferred visible forms lack an extra initial ad-. The 1v/3v lemma repetitions support aptatione/aptationes.
uncertainty_apparatus.semantic_limit: Do not silently adopt adaptatione/adaptationes from a different printed recension.

uncertainty_apparatus.evidence: A possible h after initial t is unresolved; telesmi/thelesmi retained as spelling alternatives.
uncertainty_apparatus.semantic_limit: The obscure loan term is not assigned an assured technical substance or translated as a confirmed ordinary noun.

uncertainty_apparatus.evidence: A following contraction may be que; its attachment/reading is not fully secure. Main reading retains the uncertainty.
uncertainty_apparatus.semantic_limit: Gentleness and great ingenium are both present regardless; no change to object identity inferred.

uncertainty_apparatus.evidence: The compact verb is not securely expanded. Habuit is the present preferred visual reading, with habebit plausible if the abbreviation is expanded otherwise. Habebis is not silently installed from the familiar text. The 3v commentary has a compact related glory phrase but does not securely settle the main-text ending here.
uncertainty_apparatus.semantic_limit: Person and tense, hence whether the implied ascending thing or addressed reader receives glory, remain unresolved.

uncertainty_apparatus.evidence: Preferred reading includes the que contraction after ideo; no source-neutral reduction to ideo.
uncertainty_apparatus.semantic_limit: The effect on obscurity is linked to preceding content, but the causal scope is not uniquely delimited.

uncertainty_apparatus.evidence: Sicut is the preferred actual first word. The following abbreviated sign is provisionally expanded ergo. The 3v lemma repeats the world-creation clause but need not repeat every connective.
uncertainty_apparatus.semantic_limit: Do not silently replace the whole phrase by familiar Sic mundus creatus est; assertion/comparison syntax remains somewhat open.

uncertainty_apparatus.evidence: The compressed reading is provisionally expanded modus. A short mos-like written form is visible; the exact contraction requires further palaeographic adjudication.
uncertainty_apparatus.semantic_limit: The manner/method reference points here without unambiguously naming a numbered operation.

uncertainty_apparatus.reading: Hermes, tres totius mundi partes habens sapientie
uncertainty_apparatus.evidence: Hermes is expanded from its contracted spelling. Tres is separately written before the three-parts clause. No explicit Trismegistus appears in this main-text phrase.
uncertainty_apparatus.semantic_limit: Three parts of wisdom are claimed, but this body does not enumerate which three. Their later commentary identification is not imported into the Tabula.

uncertainty_apparatus.evidence: Et lune is directly present, not added editorially. This is a Sun-and-Moon ending, not a Solis-only one.
uncertainty_apparatus.semantic_limit: The closing statement reports completion of what the speaker said about the operation, not proven completion of a physical operation.

uncertainty_apparatus.evidence: A visibly crossed/overworked letter group lies before aptatione. It can look fuit-like, but neither its exact prior reading nor cancellation status is fully secure. The normalized reading treats it provisionally as a correction trace, shown explicitly rather than silently erased.
uncertainty_apparatus.semantic_limit: If this is an active word rather than deleted writing, the clause needs further adjudication. No new certain verb or automatic sentence completion is supplied.

content_outline.latin_anchor: Philosophus dicit; verum sine mendacio, certum verissimum
content_outline.meaning: Ein Philosoph wird als Sprecher eingeführt; es folgt ein Wahrheits- und Gewissheitsanspruch.
content_outline.remaining_limit: Der Sprecherrahmen ist Textinhalt, kein experimenteller Beweis. Hermes wird erst am Ende ausdrücklich genannt.

content_outline.latin_anchor: quod est superius ... inferius; quod est inferius ... superius; ad penetranda miracula unius rei
content_outline.meaning: Zuerst wird das Obere mit dem Unteren verglichen, danach das Untere mit dem Oberen; Zweckbezug zu den Wundern einer Sache.
content_outline.remaining_limit: Sicut behauptet Entsprechung, nicht zwingend numerische Identität. Was die eine Sache ist, bleibt unbenannt.

content_outline.latin_anchor: omnes res ab uno fuerunt meditatione unius
content_outline.meaning: Alles wird auf einen Ursprung und die meditatione eines Einen bezogen.
content_outline.remaining_limit: Ab uno und unius müssen nicht ohne Begründung derselbe Stoff, dieselbe Person oder Gott sein.

content_outline.latin_anchor: et sicut nate fuerunt res omnes ab hac re una aptatione
content_outline.meaning: Alle Dinge werden als aus dieser einen Sache durch Aptation entstanden beschrieben.
content_outline.remaining_limit: Die Korrektur bleibt Teil des Befunds; ein einzelner realer Herstellungsablauf folgt daraus nicht automatisch.

content_outline.latin_anchor: pater eius sol, mater eius luna
content_outline.meaning: Sonne und Mond erhalten die Rollen Vater und Mutter des mit eius Bezeichneten.
content_outline.remaining_limit: Der Possessor ist grammatisch nicht durch einen Eigennamen neu festgelegt; Elternschaft kann metaphorisch sein.

content_outline.latin_anchor: portavit illud ventus in ventre suo
content_outline.meaning: Wind trug das mit illud Bezeichnete in seinem Bauch.
content_outline.remaining_limit: Suo bindet zunächst den Bauch an den Wind; der getragene Gegenstand wird nicht neu benannt. Kein Gefäßmodell ergänzen.
Eine Nährerrolle ist nicht gleich einem geschriebenen Einlagerungs- oder Mengenschritt.

content_outline.latin_anchor: pater omnis t[h?]elesmi totius mundi est hic
content_outline.meaning: Hic wird Vater allen telesmus/thelesmus der ganzen Welt genannt.
content_outline.remaining_limit: Pater wiederholt eine Rolle aus T05, ohne dadurch denselben Vaterreferenten festzulegen. Telesmi bleibt lexikalisch unsicher.

content_outline.latin_anchor: vis eius integra est si versa fuerit in terram
content_outline.meaning: Die Kraft ist vollständig, falls sie/das Gemeinte in Erde verwandelt worden ist.
content_outline.remaining_limit: Der Bezug des femininen versa kann zur vis oder zum ungenannten Gegenstand gehören; weder Kondition noch Transformation weglassen.

content_outline.latin_anchor: separabis terram ab igne, subtile a spisso, suaviter[que?] cum magno ingenio
content_outline.meaning: Der Angeredete wird Erde von Feuer sowie das Feine vom Dichten trennen; Sanftheit und großes Geschick/ingenium qualifizieren den Vorgang.
content_outline.remaining_limit: Zwei Trennverhältnisse sind geschrieben. Sie sind nicht ohne Begründung vier getrennte Stoffportionen oder zwei unabhängige Versuche.

content_outline.latin_anchor: ascendit a terra in celum, iterumque descendit in terram
content_outline.meaning: Ein nicht erneut benanntes Subjekt steigt von Erde in den Himmel und steigt wieder zur Erde herab.
content_outline.remaining_limit: Gerichtete Folge und Rückkehr sind Textinhalt. Physische Stoffidentität, Gesamtmenge und wörtlicher Ort bleiben offen.

content_outline.meaning: Das implizite Subjekt empfängt die Kraft des Oberen und Unteren.
content_outline.remaining_limit: Der Bezug zu den oberen/unteren Entsprechungen ist inhaltlich möglich, aber keine im Text nummerierte Objektgleichung.

content_outline.meaning: Glorie der ganzen Welt wird als Wirkung/Zustand genannt.
content_outline.remaining_limit: Die genaue Verbform, Person und Zeit sind ungeklärt; kein sicherer Wechsel zur zweiten Person durch habebis behauptet.

content_outline.latin_anchor: ideoque fugiet a te omnis obscuritas
content_outline.meaning: Alle Dunkelheit wird vom angesprochenen Du fliehen.
content_outline.remaining_limit: Te ist ausdrücklich zweite Person; nicht still dasselbe physische Objekt wie das Aufsteigende.

content_outline.latin_anchor: fortitudinis fortis fortitudo; vincet ... subtilem; solidam penetrabit
content_outline.meaning: Eine herausgehobene Stärke wird behauptet und damit begründet, dass sie alles Feine besiegt und alles Feste durchdringt.
content_outline.remaining_limit: Vincet und penetrabit sind verschiedene Prädikate. Bildliche und wörtliche Wirksamkeit bleiben offen; kein moderner Stofftest folgt.
Das unsichere Konnektiv und sicut dürfen nicht zu einem zusätzlichen Imperativ Erschaffe die Welt umgedeutet werden.

content_outline.latin_anchor: hinc erunt aptationes mirabiles, quarum [modus?] hic est
content_outline.meaning: Von hieraus werden wunderbare Aptationen/Anwendungen erwartet; ihre Art/Methode sei hier.
content_outline.remaining_limit: Hinc/hic sind Rückverweise mit offenem Umfang. Kein nummerierter Rücksprung oder exakt definierter Teilalgorithmus steht da.

content_outline.latin_anchor: itaque vocatus sum Hermes; tres ... partes habens sapientie
content_outline.meaning: Der Sprecher nennt sich Hermes und beansprucht drei Teile der Weisheit der ganzen Welt.
content_outline.remaining_limit: Erste Person ist ausdrücklich geschrieben; tres ist keine ausgeschriebene Namensform Trismegistus. Die drei Teile sind im Hauptblock nicht aufgezählt.

content_outline.latin_anchor: completum est quod dixi de operatione solis et lune
content_outline.meaning: Abgeschlossen sei, was der Sprecher über die Operation von Sonne und Mond gesagt hat.
content_outline.remaining_limit: Metatextueller Abschluss mit beiden Gestirnen; keine historische Durchführung oder fertige materielle Ausbeute behaupten.

speaker_and_reference_limits: Philosophus dicit introduces reported speech. The first-person Hermes claim and dixi close that speech; no historical author identity is thereby established.

Second-person separabis and a te address someone. Ascendit/descendit/recipit have an unexpressed third-person subject. The glory verb remains uncertain. These grammatical roles are not silently collapsed into one physical object.
Unius rei, ab uno, meditatione unius, hac re una, eius, illud, hic and vis eius form a connected discourse but do not uniquely establish one immutable material token.

Suo in ventre suo most directly belongs to ventus. Pater recurs with different stated relations; terra recurs as nurse, condition/result, separated item and source/destination. Repeated lexical form does not erase role changes.
Telesmi, meditatione, aptatione, ingenio, obscuritas and sapientia may bear technical, cosmological or allegorical senses. No single modern chemical mechanism is fixed here.
Ascent then renewed descent and reception of both powers are written. No mass, vessel, number of repetitions, lossless return or identified laboratory material is supplied.
The final solis et lune reprises both parental luminaries, but a model equating every mention with literal astronomical bodies or with particular metals would require a declared interpretation.
The main text says three parts of wisdom without listing them. Any mineral/vegetable/animal interpretation from the commentary is a later explanatory layer, not a replacement main-text clause.

scope_boundary.opening_owned: Philosophus dicit: Verum sine mendacio, certum verissimum.
scope_boundary.closing_owned: Completum est quod dixi de operatione solis et lune.
scope_boundary.body_inclusion: All intervening main-text clauses, including truth assertion, cosmogony, parental and nursing metaphors, condition, separation, movement, effects, three-parts self-attribution and completion statement.
scope_boundary.paratext_exclusion: Upper red title remains only partly read and is separately recorded; Expositio and the following commentary are outside the complete main-body transcription.
scope_boundary.no_critical_edition_claim: Complete coverage does not make the uncertain abbreviation expansions secure. Selected same-codex commentary repetitions are collation aids, not independent witnesses.

recurrence_vs_identity.observed: The paired upper/lower comparative vocabulary returns in inflected forms. The first pair is stated twice with reversed comparison direction.
recurrence_vs_identity.not_licensed: No equation automatically identifies upper with celum, lower with terra, or every upper/lower occurrence with one fixed physical object.

recurrence_vs_identity.observed: Earth is nurse, conditional transformation result, separated item, movement source and return destination.
recurrence_vs_identity.not_licensed: The repeated lexeme does not by itself decide literal matter versus place versus allegory, or one conserved portion across these roles.

recurrence_vs_identity.family: vis / vim versus fortitudinis / fortis / fortitudo
recurrence_vs_identity.observed: Vis and vim are inflections of one noun. Fortitudinis and fortitudo are inflections of another, with related adjective fortis in the emphatic phrase.
recurrence_vs_identity.not_licensed: Do not merge vis with fortitudo as one lexical atom or erase the emphatic repetition; neither wording alone establishes three different physical forces.

recurrence_vs_identity.family: rei / res / re / rem and unus-family forms
recurrence_vs_identity.observed: One thing, all things, this one thing, every subtle thing and every solid thing have different quantifiers and constructions. Ab uno and meditatione unius also occur.
recurrence_vs_identity.not_licensed: Lexical recurrence is not token identity. The first one, the origin, the one whose meditation is invoked, all things, and the later universal object classes cannot be coindexed without an explicit interpretation.

recurrence_vs_identity.observed: Pater is predicated twice with different stated complements. Both parental luminary nouns recur in the final operation phrase.
recurrence_vs_identity.not_licensed: The second father is not thereby the Sun; the closing operation is not a second written birth event. Repeated Sun/Moon vocabulary does not establish literal astronomy or particular metals.

recurrence_vs_identity.observed: The subtle adjective recurs in separation and overcoming. Dense and solid are different written adjectives.
recurrence_vs_identity.not_licensed: Do not conflate spissus with solidus or equate the separated subtle portion with every subtle thing later overcome.

recurrence_vs_identity.family: penetranda / penetrabit; miracula / mirabiles; aptatione / aptationes
recurrence_vs_identity.observed: The preferred penetrate-verb reading recurs with different objects and syntax. Wonder vocabulary is related but not identical; singular instrumental aptatione and plural aptationes recur.
recurrence_vs_identity.not_licensed: Do not replace penetranda with perpetranda or reduce the later clauses to a second copy of the first purpose. Wonder/aptation recurrences do not assign a shared material stock.

recurrence_vs_identity.observed: World and totality language recurs under different predicates: origin, telesmus fatherhood, glory, strength, creation and wisdom.
recurrence_vs_identity.not_licensed: Retain the repeated emphatic scope; do not replace all occurrences by one unstated shorthand or identify all quantified domains.

recurrence_vs_identity.family: eius / illud / suo; hic / hinc; implicit subjects
recurrence_vs_identity.observed: Several anaphoric and deictic constructions occur. Suo in ventre suo most directly refers to ventus. Third-person movement and reception clauses omit a new overt subject.
recurrence_vs_identity.not_licensed: The exact antecedents and scope of hic/hinc remain interpretations; similar short forms need not all denote one object or one numbered step.

recurrence_vs_identity.observed: Second-person address and later first-person self-attribution/completion are written. The glory verb remains uncertain.
recurrence_vs_identity.not_licensed: Do not turn the whole passage into a single imperative program or collapse speaker, addressee and moving subject.

interpretive_alternatives.what_it_preserves: Separation, ascent, descent, power reception, parental/nursing roles and outcome clauses must all remain.
interpretive_alternatives.open_debt: No substance, vessel, mass, repetition count or lossless transfer is explicitly assigned; metaphoric terms and pronouns require interpretations.

interpretive_alternatives.what_it_preserves: Upper/lower correspondence, one-origin claims, world creation and wisdom attribution remain as written alongside the practical-looking commands.
interpretive_alternatives.open_debt: Cannot delete separation or directed ascent/descent merely because a figurative interpretation is preferred.

interpretive_alternatives.reading: Reported teaching followed by first-person authoritative closure
interpretive_alternatives.what_it_preserves: Philosophus dicit, second-person address and Hermes/dixi self-attribution are all represented.
interpretive_alternatives.open_debt: The text does not uniquely mark every speaker transition; the uncertain glory verb prevents a secure person/tense assignment at that point.
